goal: complete work using the least disruptive eligible authority while preserving evidence and recovery capability

disruptionLevels.none: No interaction with the user's visible desktop or active physical console.
disruptionLevels.isolated-ui: UI automation runs in an isolated/headless/separate browser context and should not take focus from the user's active application.
disruptionLevels.foreground-ui: Automation may change focus or manipulate a visible application in the current user session.
disruptionLevels.physical-console: Keyboard, pointer or KVM input targets the real workstation console and can interrupt the human user.
disruptionLevels.recovery-impact: Power, reboot, virtual media or other recovery action can interrupt workloads and requires the strongest governance.
disruptionLevels.external-fallback: External remote-control interoperability used only after the owning native EVAVO route is unavailable or insufficient.

routeOrder.rule: Use when a typed native interface can complete the task.

Preferred shared agent ingress for authenticated logical storage mutation, EVAVO Storage bridge work, route health and bounded workstation control. The gateway delegates bytes to Local Storage and execution to the appropriate execution authority; it does not become a second byte store or generic shell.

Preferred route for code, Git, file, build, test, package, process, service and local-model work when the singleton gateway does not expose the required typed operation. Windows non-interactive child processes should use hidden/no-console launch policy.

Direct specialist MCP is an independent route for capabilities not available through the singleton gateway. MCP stdio remains attached to client pipes. Do not detach protocol processes merely to hide a console.
Prefer headless or isolated browser context before native desktop interaction when the web workflow supports it.
Use only when a real desktop application/UI must be manipulated. Declare focus disruption and keep the interaction bounded.

Use governed S3 HID only when narrower in-band routes cannot perform the required physical-console interaction and the signed operation gate is green. For workstation control-plane recovery, the only supported bootstrap target is BOOTSTRAP-EVAVO-REMOTE-CONTROL-V6.ps1 with its exact confirmation phrase; never type or invoke retired queue installers directly.

Prefer observation over interaction. Effectful Comet KVM is an escalation/recovery path and requires exact provider admission and action governance. If console recovery is required, invoke the single V6 remote-control bootstrap rather than individual legacy task/queue installers.

Power, reset and virtual-media operations are last-resort native EVAVO recovery and must not be selected for routine work. After machine/session recovery, restore the software control plane only through the V6 remote-control bootstrap and require its fresh Current durable-intent proof.

Optional convenience/recovery fallback only after the owning native EVAVO route is unavailable or insufficient. Its availability never defines MSI health, its failure never means the workstation is offline, and its results require reconciliation through the owning EVAVO authority before physical completion is claimed.

s3_comet.meaning: Stage 1 signed workstation physical-control profile while C5 is absent.

full.meaning: Full signed hardware profile. C5 is passive telemetry by default.

clientRules.chatgpt-pro: Use connected/native tools first, then the authenticated singleton gateway when registered and healthy, then other native EVAVO routes by declared order. Desktop Commander is external fallback interoperability only. Local MCP capabilities require explicit client registration and a newly negotiated/reconnected tool session; repository presence alone is not connectivity.
clientRules.claude-code: Prefer the singleton gateway for shared storage/control operations, then Local Compute/direct specialist MCP before interactive terminal or desktop control. Desktop Commander is fallback only.
clientRules.codex: Prefer the singleton gateway for shared storage/control operations, then Local Compute/direct specialist MCP and isolated browser control before actual-console routes. Desktop Commander is fallback only.
clientRules.api-agent: Select the first eligible native EVAVO route by this policy and retain receipts for effectful work. Use Desktop Commander only when native route eligibility is exhausted for the requested operation.

healthRules: Health and self-heal should use status endpoints, process/service APIs and watchdogs before GUI interaction.
Storage route health must distinguish logical gateway readiness, Local Storage writer readiness, BeeStation primary-writer readiness and Windows execution fallback readiness.
A watchdog may restart only owned processes according to its repository contract; watchdog recovery must not silently send HID or change hardware identity.
Network Studio owns private Comet LAN/Tailscale reachability and failover diagnosis.
A failed transport describes that transport only. Do not infer machine power/offline state without independent machine-level evidence.
Before declaring local execution unavailable, evaluate all native EVAVO routes capable of the requested operation.
Desktop Commander is external fallback only and is not required for local verification.
Escalate to physical-console or OOB recovery only after narrower in-band paths are unavailable or insufficient.
Any S3/Comet/OOB software-plane recovery must converge through BOOTSTRAP-EVAVO-REMOTE-CONTROL-V6.ps1 and may claim success only after the Current queue emits a fresh durable invocation receipt.

Task Scheduler accepting Start-ScheduledTask, a GitHub issue becoming closed, a transport returning 2xx, or a generic process exiting 0 may establish transport/progress evidence only; none of them alone proves that the intended physical postcondition occurred.
After execution may have begun, any missing, degraded, contradictory or unrecognized terminal receipt requires postcondition reconciliation before re-executing the underlying action.
